analysis: The PR contains only documentation and a changelog entry (changelog.d/flint-paged-only-defaults.md; docs/architecture/inference.md hunk at base 2058-2069, head 2058-2077). No executable code is supplied, so no authorization, attestation, encryption or billing control changes are visible. The docs describe a Swift-side behavior change that is not in this batch: Flint (a) ignores provider-wide checkpoint 'balanced' defaults in EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve and still refuses explicit non-native selections, and (b) is served only on paged attention, with EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend treating automatic KV selection as explicit paged. An explicit contiguous selection, the paged kill switch, a crash-loop guard or a capability veto refuses the load rather than degrading. This is a fail-closed posture and narrows the previously documented automatic fallback to contiguous. Relevant threat areas are TB-007 and T-041 (prefix cache and the KV path), plus availability. The refusal on kill switch or crash-loop could reduce availability for Flint, but that is a deliberate design choice and is not a security regression. Unverified contracts for the next pass: the actual code implementing these claims (EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve, prepareProductionBackend, ModelBenchmark.usesNativeGeneration, ThroughputSweep.measuresScalarPrefill) is not supplied, so the docs' accuracy cannot be confirmed. Also unconfirmed is whether the paged path preserves the encrypted SSD prefix-cache scoping (cacheSalt, HMAC tags) that T-041 relies on. The doc patch excerpt was truncated, but the supplied base text covers the earlier part of the file only; the Flint section at lines ~2055+ is not visible in base_text, so no citation was made. The end-of-hunk text is cut off, so it is not fully reviewed. No findings.
